career_ladder.note: Judicial officers in the State of Bihar are governed by the Bihar Judicial Service Rules and the Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) framework instituted under the directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in All India Judges Association v. Union of India (WP (C) No. 643/2015). Pay progression combines Assured Career Progression (ACP) time-scales and cadre promotional vacancies to Senior Civil Judge and District Judge cadres.

exam_scheme.note: BPSC conducts the Bihar Judicial Service Competitive Examination in three successive stages: Preliminary Examination (Objective screening, 250 marks), Main Written Examination (Descriptive, 1050 marks across 5 compulsory and 3 optional papers), and Viva-Voce (Interview, 100 marks with a mandatory 35% qualifying threshold).

financial_package.note: State judicial officers in Bihar do not draw central 7th CPC civil salaries; they are governed by the Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) Pay Matrix Level J-1 implemented pursuant to Supreme Court orders in All India Judges Association v. Union of India.
financial_package.pay_source_label: Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) Pay Matrix Table for Subordinate Judicial Officers
financial_package.estimate_note: Range assumes Level J-1 entry basic pay of ₹77,840 at project standard 58% DA (effective 1 Jul 2025). Emoluments include judicial allowance, HRA (8% to 18% based on Patna or district posting), sumptuary allowance, and medical benefits. In-hand estimates reflect standard deductions including 10% NPS contribution and applicable income tax.
official_perks: Official rent-free government bungalow / judicial quarters or designated leased housing
Official staff vehicle with fuel allowance and designated official driver
Comprehensive medical coverage for officer, spouse, and dependent family members
Robe allowance, library/book grant, and residential telephone/broadband allowance
Armed security guard and orderlies at official residence and courtroom
